Now, a model-based analysis shows that pretreating end-of-life batteries is critical for enhancing the sustainability of recycling.

records.title: Blue carbon ecosystems and coral reefs as coupled nature-based climate solutions
records.description: Coral reefs are at a planetary tipping point, widely threatened by ocean acidification. Preserving and promoting coastal ecosystems can align with existing nature-based solutions to bolster blue carbon reservoirs to increase ocean alkalinity and support coral reef restoration.

records.title: Impacts of pretreatment routes on spent lithium-ion batteries recycling
records.description: Pretreatment is a prerequisite to recycle spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and advance resource circularity, but its impacts on the overall performance and environmental footprint of LIBs recycling are poorly understood. This study develops unit-level models to address this knowledge gap.

records.title: Race out to eco-friendly peptide synthesis
records.description: The growing demand for therapeutic peptides has intensified concerns about the sustainability of current synthetic processes, which typically rely on excess reagents and, most critically, large volumes of solvents. In the pursuit of more sustainable practices, scientists now report a water-based synthetic protocol.

records.title: Water-based coupling of amino acids for sustainable solid-phase peptide synthesis
records.description: The growing market demand for peptides is drawing more attention to their industrial synthetic procedures, which rely on large amounts of toxic solvents. Here the authors suggest practical steps that bring fully water-based peptide synthesis closer to reality.

records.title: Technology flexibility and sobriety to address shortage of energy-transition metals
records.description: Metals shortage threatens climate goals by affecting adoption of key technologies for the energy transition. Optimizing technology mixes is now shown to limit the supply-constrained energy transition metals to only copper, lithium, and vanadium, though economy-wide resource sobriety remains urgent.

records.title: One Health synergies
records.description: Linking humans, animals, plants, environments and ecosystems to forge healthier lives on a healthier planet clearly aligns with sustainability objectives. A collection of research and opinion presents ideas on the way forward to support such alignment.

records.title: Global evidence synthesis on land-use change and zoonotic risks
records.description: Land-use change, among other anthropogenic factors, has led to increased levels of zoonotic disease transmission. The authors assess how land-use change and restoration activities impact zoonotic disease transmission, providing an online tool useful for One Health-oriented restoration planning.

records.title: Towards One Health action for addressing antimicrobial resistance in the age of polycrisis
records.description: Antimicrobial resistance continues to be a critical One Health challenge, despite research and policy progress. Building on the past decade of research, this Perspective provides an integrative roadmap for addressing antimicrobial resistance by leveraging the complexities of human and environment interactions.

records.title: Livestock antimicrobial use embodied in global supply chains
records.description: Excessive antimicrobial use can increase the threat of antimicrobial resistance; however, how such use is embedded in global trade is still unclear. Authors here estimate global livestock antimicrobial footprints through global supply chains to better understand and manage antimicrobial use.

records.title: Livestock antimicrobial use embodied in global supply chains
records.description: Excessive antimicrobial use can increase the threat of antimicrobial resistance; however, how such use is embedded in global trade is still unclear. Authors here estimate global livestock antimicrobial footprints through global supply chains to better understand and manage antimicrobial use.

records.title: Macroecological approaches for the prediction of zoonotic disease risk
records.description: In recent decades, zoonotic disease outbreaks have become increasingly frequent, necessitating strategies to improve the accuracy of predictive modelling. This Review discusses the importance of macroecological variables in such modelling efforts to improve preparedness for future potential outbreaks.

records.title: A field‑deployable CRISPR-based biosensing platform for monitoring marine ecosystems
records.description: Human impacts on marine ecosystems are increasing the likelihood of pathogenic outbreaks, harmful algal blooms and coral stress. Here the authors develop a CRISPR biomonitoring tool that can help detect key marine species that are important to public health, the aquaculture sector and marine ecosystems.

records.title: Integrating materials innovation and policy challenges for leather alternatives
records.description: The leather industry is at a pivotal moment on its path towards sustainability. Although many bio-based leather alternatives can reduce environmental impact, we need clear definitions of such alternatives to guide materials innovations that truly bring them into the mainstream, sustainable market, as highlighted in a recent court ruling.

records.title: Global gridded dataset of heating and cooling degree days under climate change scenarios
records.description: Accurate projections of heating and cooling needs are vital for planning energy use and achieving the sustainable development goals. A global dataset now maps global heating and cooling degree days, finding future hotspots, rising cooling demand and early shifts in energy needs with major global impacts.

records.title: Levers for equitable material use
records.description: Global household material use is highly unequal: the top 10% drive roughly a third of footprints and most of the overshoot beyond safe limits. Curbing affluent overconsumption, while securing decent material floors, should be a central policy lever to cut material demand quickly and fairly.

records.title: Consumption inequalities in material use undermining resources sustainability
records.description: Global material use is rising unsustainably, but its distribution across individuals remains unclear. A study now reveals deep inequality in household material footprints, especially for non-renewable resources, and suggests that curbing overconsumption among the wealthy is key to sustainability.

records.title: Biochar boom-and-bust cycle
Safeguarding, strengthening and expanding river protections for nature and people
records.description: River protection in the United States remains scant, with just over one-tenth of river length in the contiguous states protected at viable levels, often by land-based protection measures that fail to capture the full diversity of the nation’s river systems. There is an urgent need for policies that safeguard, strengthen and expand freshwater protections to secure rivers that sustain both people and nature.

records.title: Global habitat hotspots and extinction vulnerability of terrestrial vertebrates
records.description: The threat of species extinction is a major problem resulting from various anthropogenic pressures. Here the authors use deep learning models and ecological network theory to study the impacts of human pressures on terrestrial vertebrate habitat hotspots now and under future scenarios of global change.

records.title: National assessment of river protection in the United States
records.description: Although river protection is core to social and environmental well-being, the extent to which river conservation policies are effective is difficult to assess. This study reveals that, under all relevant protection mechanisms in the contiguous USA, only 12% of rivers are adequately protected.

records.title: Meta-analytical evidence of a self–other discrepancy in climate change-related risk perceptions
records.description: People tend to perceive their personal risk from climate change as lower than the risk faced by others, which can demotivate engaging in mitigation actions. A meta-analysis now quantifies this perception gap, showing that its global and regional variation depends on who the ‘other’ is.

records.title: Energy-efficient indirect (bi)carbonate electroreduction in a porous solid electrolyte reactor
records.description: Reactive carbon capture enables CO 2 conversion into valuable chemicals without the typically separate energy-intensive CO 2 recovery step. In this work, the authors suggest minimizing its performance trade-offs via indirect bicarbonate conversion within a porous solid electrolyte reactor.

records.title: Fast and selective CO 2 capture from outdoor air by covalent organic frameworks
records.description: Direct air capture is a promising technology to mitigate the rising atmospheric CO 2 concentrations contributing to climate change. Here a covalent organic framework with high CO 2 capacity and cycling stability is reported to be capable of selectively and rapidly removing CO 2 from open air.

records.title: Climate change-driven contaminants in water
records.description: Climate change creates multiple pathways of water contamination. Here we call for defining climate change-driven contaminants as a distinct class and explore their implications.

records.title: Social factors shape federal environmental crime prosecution patterns in the USA
records.description: This study analyses the geographic patterns of US federal environmental crime prosecutions over 2011–2020, showing that, on average, they tend to occur more in counties with higher socioeconomic status than in the most environmentally degraded areas of the USA.

records.title: Cross-system cascades as drivers of the electrification pathway in net-zero transitions
records.description: Positive cross-system cascades in sustainability transitions are underexplored, despite their potential to accelerate net-zero pathways. This Perspective analyses such cascades in the context of electrification, identifying 12 mechanisms across sociotechnical systems and offering policy recommendations to amplify their impact.

records.title: Unravelling the threads of microfibre terminology
records.description: Although researchers try to understand the physical and chemical impacts of fibre-shaped microscopic pollution, use of inconsistent terminology hinders collective progress. Here we call for a unified language as the essential foundation for coordinated research across disciplines and effective mitigation.

records.title: Effects of forestry decentralization on rural inequality in Nepal
records.description: Decentralized natural resource governance is thought to aid conservation and reduce poverty, but its heterogeneous local effects are under-explored. A study in Nepal shows that forest governance decentralization reduces poverty but the benefits are greater for dominant ethnic and caste groups compared with minority ones.

records.title: Bridging the fuel tax revenue gap in the move to electric mobility
records.description: Governments worldwide collected US$923 billion in fuel taxes in 2023, revenues at risk with the transition to electric vehicles, especially in lower-income countries. Policymakers should anticipate and assess their own domestic exposure and develop policies to recover enough revenues from electric vehicles as the transition progresses.

records.title: The electric vehicle transition and vanishing fuel tax revenues
records.description: As electric vehicle adoption rises, governments face shrinking fuel tax revenues without clear replacement policies. This study estimates this revenue loss across 168 countries and finds that lower-income nations are the most exposed and may need international support to manage the fiscal risks.

records.title: Halving global ammonia emissions with cost-effective measures
records.description: Man-made ammonia emissions have harmful effects on human health and ecosystems, yet global mitigation strategies remain underexploited. A study now finds that emissions could be halved cost-effectively by 2050 through targeted and prioritized measures, with benefits far outweighing costs.

records.title: Holistic evaluation for deployment
records.description: Thermoelectric technologies can convert waste heat directly into clean electricity, but high laboratory efficiency does not necessarily translate into practical deployment. By revisiting the long-neglected material zinc antimonide, researchers now show that strong thermoelectric performance can go hand in hand with affordability and sustainability.

records.title: Assessing the carbon emissions and energy consumption of US hyperscale data centres
records.description: The growing number of hyperscale data centres raises concerns about their environmental impacts. This study presents a facility-resolved attributional framework to assess the carbon footprint of hyperscale data centres in the USA using plant-level electricity-generation and emissions data.

records.title: Unlocking sustainable thermoelectric generation with zinc antimonide
records.description: Thermoelectric technologies must balance conversion efficiency with resource sustainability. Here the authors demonstrate that eco-friendly zinc antimonide (ZnSb) is a viable materials choice, delivering ~8% efficiency alongside exceptional cost-effectiveness.

records.title: Towards practical photosynthetic biohybrid systems
records.description: Photosynthetic biohybrid systems can convert sunlight to chemicals and fuels. This Perspective explores how to better design photosynthetic biohybrid systems to achieve practical sustainable solar-driven biomanufacturing.

records.title: Robust hydrogel ion channels for osmotic energy harvesting and environmental sensing
records.description: Salinity gradient blue energy offers a promising alternative to fossil fuels. Here the authors develop ultrarough, self-healing hydrogel ionic conductors that achieve an excellent power density while maintaining over 91% of their performance after damage and enable autonomous environmental sensing.

records.title: Cost-effective climate change mitigation through land sector contributions
records.description: Land-based mitigation can substantially lower the cost of climate action and ease energy sector decarbonization. Modelled pathways show that limiting warming to 1.5 °C becomes unattainable without land sector contributions, although sustainability trade-offs require careful policy design.

records.title: Widespread North American pollution and health impacts from early twentieth century copper production
records.description: Mining and industrial emissions can be substantially reduced by technological interventions. The historical case of copper production in Anaconda, Montana shows the widespread health burdens that can result when lax regulation delays such interventions.

records.title: Agricultural data source choice as a dominant control on nitrogen surplus uncertainty
records.description: Environmental impacts from nitrogen surplus in agricultural regions make it critical to understand the nature and drivers of excess nitrogen. Bhaduri and colleagues show that data source uncertainty must be accounted for to avoid misalignments in management and mitigation decisions.

records.title: A socio-economic resilience metric shifts disaster risk priorities
records.description: Using microsimulations, we quantify disaster-related decreases in material well-being, capturing not only what is damaged, but also how damage affects the population. We calculate socio-economic resilience — a population’s capacity to maintain well-being despite asset damages — and find that global well-being losses exceed US$1 trillion annually, representing about double the monetary asset damages.

records.title: Making ammonia at the water’s edge
records.description: Photocatalytic nitrogen fixation can make ammonia from nitrogen and water under mild conditions, but slow nitrogen delivery and product build-up limit output. Now, a floating solar interface couples nitrogen reduction with evaporation, greatly speeding up ammonia formation and concentrating a high-purity product in the condensate.

records.title: Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction to high-concentration ammonia via interfacial evaporation
records.description: Synthesis of valuable ammonia through photocatalytic reduction of nitrogen is a promising sustainable route, but its efficiency remains limited. This work shows that coupling the reaction with solar-driven interfacial evaporation can substantially improve ammonia yield, concentration and purity.

records.title: Far-right slows energy transition
records.description: Political identity is known to shape climate attitudes, but its effect on real-world adoption of clean technologies has been unclear. Now, data from Germany show that rising far-right support slows the uptake of rooftop solar and electric cars. However, these effects are not large enough to stall the transition.

records.title: The SDGs need a subjective well-being reality check
records.description: The Sustainable Development Goals aim to improve lives, but it is unclear whether progress on Sustainable Development Goal indicators translates into greater subjective well-being over time. A study of 42 countries found associations in levels, but weak links with year-to-year changes in life evaluations.

records.title: On living and feeling better
records.description: As the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) enter their final years, there is a desire to reflect on their societal impact. A study now compares changes in the SDG indicators with changes in how people feel about their lives and finds no detectable correlation between the two.

records.title: Global socio-economic resilience to disasters
records.description: Disaster risk assessments often overlook how damages affect well-being and recovery across populations. A global analysis now shows that well-being losses from disasters are much higher than asset damages, with the poorest suffering disproportionately.

records.title: Author Correction: Urban energy and transport impacts of autonomous robotaxi deployment
Adapting to the risk of Atlantic circulation change
records.description: Weakening Atlantic circulation could shift temperatures and rainfall across continents, raise regional sea levels, disrupt food production and marine ecosystems, and erode the ocean carbon sink. Planning in the most exposed countries does not yet account for these risks; we propose five steps to close this blind spot.

records.title: A thin carbon membrane to capture carbon
records.description: Anthropogenic emissions are rapidly increasing atmospheric CO 2 levels, with severe consequences for the global climate. Researchers have developed a carbon membrane as thin as only two molecular layers that sieves and captures CO 2 with very high flux and selectivity, holding promise for climate change mitigation technologies.

records.title: Recyclable flow battery chemistry
records.description: Turning water-based flow batteries into a truly sustainable technology hinges on recycling the organic molecules inside the battery. A redox-active organic molecule has now been developed that not only outperforms the industry-standard vanadium benchmark but also offers exceptional reusability.

records.title: A circular oligo(disulfide) anolyte enables practical aqueous redox flow batteries
records.description: Aqueous flow batteries are ideal for grid storage but lack sustainable, high-capacity anolytes. Here the authors report a recyclable oligo(disulfide) design that combines closed-loop recyclability with good electrochemical performance.

records.title: Efficient carbon dioxide separation with molecularly thin bilayer carbon membranes
records.description: Membrane-based separations offer a promising energy-efficient approach to mitigating CO 2 emissions. Here the authors develop molecularly thin graphene–amorphous carbon membranes that simultaneously deliver sharp molecular sieving, high permeance and mechanical stability for selective CO 2 separation.

records.title: Author Correction: Rice–fish co-culturing reduces schistosomiasis risk and increases yields and incomes
Binding dissimilar biomaterials
records.description: Biopolymer composites offer a sustainable route to multifunctional materials, but integrating chemically distinct biopolymers remains challenging owing to mismatched interfacial interactions. Now, researchers report a small molecule strategy that modulates biomass networks, improving their structural integration and functionality.

records.title: Material circularity implications of battery degradation in shared electric mobility
records.description: Shared mobility aims to save materials, yet intensive use accelerates battery degradation and may alter these savings. This study assesses the implications of shared mobility by coupling fleet projections, battery degradation and dynamic material flow analysis in China.

records.title: Artificial intelligence for life-cycle-aware sustainable materials discovery
records.description: Materials discovery by artificial intelligence rarely considers scalability, environmental impacts or end-of-life management, prioritizing functional performance. This Perspective suggests a roadmap for embedding life-cycle considerations in the discovery process to design sustainable materials from the start.

records.title: Small-molecule-bound biopolymer networks for sustainable multifunctional composites
records.description: Combining biomaterials of different nature can yield sustainable composites with otherwise inaccessible properties. This study presents a strategy to overcome interfacial mismatch between individual components, enabling efficient structural integration within mechanically strong, multifunctional films.

records.title: Quantifying assets for the geopolitics of climate change mitigation
records.description: Climate action reshapes who gains and loses from energy and environmental resources, raising new geopolitical questions. A study now quantifies four climate-related asset types across 169 countries and reveals uneven asset redistribution, with major powers often less affected.

records.title: Skill and spatial mismatches for sustainable development in Brazil
records.description: Deforestation-reducing development pathways may cut emissions, but it is unclear how workers can adapt given skill and geographic mobility constraints. Modelling job transitions in Brazil reveals that greener pathways benefit workers in high-skill occupations but increase low-skill unemployment, mitigated by mobility policies.

records.title: Assessing green-growth and degrowth pathways through institutional regime feasibility
records.description: Choosing a feasible economic growth trajectory to mitigate climate change cannot hinge on only gross domestic product trends. This Perspective presents a framework to understand where each possible growth path places its heaviest burdens and shows that such understanding is critical to inform policy decisions.

records.title: Limited agricultural gains but high flood risk from global wetland reclamation
records.description: As food demand increases, global wetlands are being reclaimed as croplands; however, these reclaimed croplands are not only less productive, but also face substantially higher flood exposure. This dual vulnerability highlights the urgency of balancing food security with wetland conservation.

records.title: Design principles for functional carbon materials derived from biomass conversion
records.description: Biomass-derived carbon materials hold great promise for various sustainable technologies. This Perspective argues that biomass composition alone is insufficient to predict material performance and proposes a conversion pathway-guided framework to optimize reactivity, transport properties and stability.

records.title: Air filters with sustained breathability
records.description: Although essential to protect human health, air purification technologies suffer from clogging, short lifespans and repeated cartridge replacements. A wet-interface filter design now addresses these challenges, enabling efficient capture of airborne pollutants while prolonging filter service time.

records.title: Highly efficient air purification by a charge-induced liquid-lined filter
records.description: High-efficiency air purification conventionally comes at the price of reduced service lifetimes or elevated operating costs. This paper presents a charge-induced liquid-lined filter that achieves ultrahigh efficiency, long-term durability and low maintenance for sustainable air purification.

records.title: Green synthesis of hydrogen and formaldehyde from methanol with enhanced quantum efficiency
records.description: Catalytic conversion of methanol to hydrogen potentially offers a safer and greener alternative to conventional hydrogen production routes. This Article presents a single-atom-based catalytic cluster that enables efficient hydrogen production from methanol with the co-generation of valuable formaldehyde instead of CO 2 .

records.title: Preparing for disasters
records.description: The impacts of extreme natural events are dramatic for both people and physical infrastructure. More can and should be done to contain the damage and prevent loss of life.

records.title: Count what can be lost at once
Himalayan hazards to high-mountain hydropower
Beyond resilience in a changing Himalaya
Restoration-driven positive and negative leakage in sub-Saharan Africa
records.description: Restoration initiatives are important for progress towards climate and biodiversity policy goals; however, whether they lead to the displacement of tree loss elsewhere (leakage effect) is still unclear. This study examines the leakage impacts of restoration projects in sub-Saharan Africa.

records.title: Navigating the land–energy nexus for carbon-neutral power systems in China
records.description: As countries expand renewable energy to reach net zero, finding suitable land is becoming increasingly challenging. A new China-wide optimization study shows that land constraints redirect renewable development, increase transmission needs and raise 2060 system costs by up to 4.1%.

records.title: An historic fishery collapse driven by socioeconomic and environmental factors
records.description: The collapse of the western Baltic herring fishery by the year 1570 caused large disruptions. Using a time series of Baltic herring catches spanning 450 years, this study examined the socioeconomic and environmental drivers of the collapse, offering lessons for fisheries management today.

records.title: Asymmetric Mo–Ni atom pairs enable scalable water oxidation at industrial current densities
records.description: Alkaline water electrolysis offers a promising pathway for green hydrogen production, but the anodic oxygen evolution reaction remains a performance bottleneck. Here the authors develop a nickel-based catalyst featuring asymmetric Mo–Ni atom pairs that enable highly stable, scalable water oxidation at industrial current densities.

records.title: Far-right political support and clean technology adoption in Germany
records.description: Political polarization may hinder the spread of clean technologies, but its influence on adoption may change over time. A study now combines surveys, municipal data and election results to show lower electric vehicle and solar photovoltaic uptake among far-right supporters, with persistent yet increasingly dynamic partisan differences in adoption.

records.title: Urban energy and transport impacts of autonomous robotaxi deployment
records.description: Autonomous robotaxis are being used in certain urban transport systems, but how they affect fleets and energy use is underexplored. A study now shows that robotaxis overlap with taxi demand but complement public transit, and optimized deployment could cut fleet size by 62.5% and energy use by 44.8%.

records.title: Sequential electronic reconstruction enables durable oxygen redox in water electrolysis
records.description: Electrocatalytic water oxidation remains a bottleneck for green hydrogen production due to efficiency limits. Here the authors show a sequential reconstruction activation strategy that overcomes these issues by decoupling oxygen-redox activity from lattice instability, enabling exciting performance.

records.title: Boosting water evaporation with clever surface design
records.description: Efficient evaporation is crucial for solar-powered water purification, resource recovery and energy utilization, yet boosting evaporation without using more energy remains challenging. Here, a smart surface on which water binds weakly, thereby enabling rapid solar evaporation, makes clean, sustainable water production more efficient.

records.title: Accelerating water desorption at heterostructure interfaces for high-rate solar evaporation
records.description: Solar interfacial evaporation is a promising solution for water purification. Here this work addresses the bottleneck of slow kinetics of water molecule desorption by constructing a dual-phase heterostructure that achieves a superior evaporation rate with excellent durability.

records.title: Minimizing climate change adaptation trade-offs in African rangelands
records.description: Changing rainfall patterns and intensity make adaptation a necessity for African pastoralists. Paired weather forecasting and risk smoothing help manage the trade-offs inherent to these adaptations.

records.title: Discovering catastrophic weather risks
records.description: Extreme weather is becoming more common as Earth’s climate changes. This Perspective argues that the most catastrophic extremes, beyond what has been previously recorded, must be considered and prepared for to avoid drastic impacts.

records.title: Higher odds of produced-water-like chemistry in groundwater vulnerable to shale gas spills
records.description: Horizontal drilling and hydraulic fracturing are a core part of the US domestic energy economy, particularly in the Appalachian region. However, surface spills occurring in areas of high hydrologic vulnerability could pose a risk to the drinking-water sources of more than 120,000 local residents.

records.title: Emissions and system-level decarbonization pathways for global petrochemical production
records.description: The petrochemical sector is a major source of greenhouse gas emissions, yet a consistent facility-level emissions inventory is missing, hindering effective sectoral decarbonization. This study fills the gap through a bottom-up and detailed assessment of 37,379 facilities globally.

records.title: Global analysis of nitrogen inputs from irrigation water to cropland
records.description: Irrigation is typically overlooked as a source of reactive nitrogen to cropland. However, nitrate-rich irrigation water constitutes a substantial portion of the global agricultural nitrogen budget that should be accounted for in fertilizer application and irrigation strategies.

records.title: 3D-printed living materials for anammox–denitrification coupling in wastewater treatment
records.description: Nitrate accumulation limits the sustainability of anammox-based nitrogen removal in wastewater treatment. This study shows that 3D-bioprinted engineered living materials with spatial confinement enable complete nitrogen removal by enhancing cross-feeding between anammox bacteria and denitrifiers.

records.title: Seagrass fisheries expose the poverty dimensions of marine conservation
records.description: The livelihood of people in poor coastal areas depends directly on local ecosystems, but such reliance is not well documented. With data from across 156 Indo-Pacific communities, this study examines the relationship between seagrass-associated fishing and household poverty.

records.title: Land-use optimization for food security, bioenergy and forest conservation in Indonesia
records.description: Balancing food and energy security is a key priority for Indonesia, but the associated land conversion could induce deforestation. This study examines how best to optimize energy security (biodiesel blend ratios of 50%) and food security (rice cropping) given land constraints and current policy.

records.title: A membraneless electrochemical system for alcohol-laden wastewater upcycling
records.description: Resource recovery from alcohol-laden wastewater remains challenging due to intrinsic limitations of current treatment technologies. This study introduces a membrane-free electrochemical system that safely and efficiently upcycles alcohol wastewater into valuable chemicals and hydrogen.

records.title: Daily exposure to fine particulate matter from traffic increases cancer mortality risk
records.description: Evidence from a multi-country analysis of 9.2 million cancer deaths suggests that traffic-sourced PM 2.5 might contribute to the short-term PM 2.5 -related cancer mortality burden to a much greater extent than would be expected from its share of total PM 2.5 concentration.

records.title: The changing economics of public lands in the USA
records.description: Debates over public land management in the USA have been divided between extractive use and environmental protection until the passage of major laws and consequent litigation cases. Through a historical lens, this Perspective shows the gradual move towards social-ecological systems management to emphasize resilience and diverse ecosystem services.

records.title: Maximizing electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction to achieve closed-loop reactive capture
records.description: Directly converting captured carbon dioxide into fuels and chemicals could make carbon capture more efficient by avoiding energy-intensive solvent regeneration. This Review discusses the reaction pathways, key challenges and strategies for achieving high carbon conversion.

records.title: Lessons learned from European land subsidence
records.description: Millions of people are impacted by land subsidence, which is accelerated by human-induced drivers. Across Europe, research and policy is focused on managing these drivers and mitigating their influence, with data and monitoring infrastructure playing a key role in tackling future challenges.

records.title: Phased fuel transition for low-carbon shipping
records.description: Along the Asia–Europe shipping corridor, biofuels offer the strongest near-term option, potentially cutting greenhouse gas emissions by 31–47%, while electrofuels become more competitive after 2040 under the International Maritime Organization Net-Zero Framework. Policymakers could therefore adopt a phased strategy that prioritizes biofuels now and prepares infrastructure for electrofuels after 2040, to avoid locking shipping into transitional fossil fuels.

records.title: Phased fuel transitions for decarbonizing the Asia–Europe Green Shipping Corridor
records.description: Shipping remains almost entirely reliant on fossil fuels, and identifying viable fuel transition pathways under evolving regulations is a key challenge. A study now evaluates 13 alternative marine fuels for the Asia–Europe corridor, revealing phased transitions shaped by policy design and timing.

records.title: Black carbon emissions and climate impacts of cost-saving Arctic transit shipping through 2050
records.description: Arctic transit routes offer economic gains from shorter voyages but increase regional black carbon deposition on snow and ice. A study now models the economic benefits and climate impacts of Arctic transit shipping through 2050, exploring the trade-offs of different policies.

records.title: Mapping hunting probability across the tropics in space and time
records.description: Hunting wildlife for food and trade purposes (for example, pets, ornaments) can contribute to species extinctions, warranting informed policy and interventions to curb overexploitation. Towards such goals, the authors here estimate the spatial footprint of hunting probability across the global tropics.

records.title: Integrating shipping growth and ballast water management to assess invasive species risks
records.description: Maritime shipping is a leading vector for marine bioinvasions, and ballast water regulations now apply to all international ships. A study now shows that growth in shipping traffic could amplify the global invasion risk to 94–900% of the 2018 baseline by 2100, even under widespread treatment compliance.

records.title: Scalable ambient fabrication of single-junction and perovskite–silicon tandem solar cells
records.description: Practical application of perovskite solar cells requires scalable fabrication in ambient environments. Here the authors introduce PNCC, a hole-transport co-polymer that enables ambient-fabricated devices to achieve certified efficiencies of 33.0% in tandem cells and 23.2% in modules.

records.title: Author Correction: Biodiversity recovery is slow following clear-cut harvest of boreal forests
Copper recovery that powers itself
records.description: Removing toxic yet valuable copper from industrial wastewater usually consumes energy and leaves low-value sludge behind. Now, a sulfur electrode is shown to selectively pluck copper from real effluent and recover it for reuse, turning a costly cleanup into a source of high-purity metal.

records.title: Sulfur-mediated electrochemical copper recovery from wastewater with net electricity generation
records.description: As the global demand for copper continues to grow, large volumes of industrial copper-containing wastewater pose substantial risks to the environment and human health. Here the authors present a strategy for recovering metallic copper from waste streams while simultaneously generating electricity.

records.title: A global atlas of soil microbial genetic resources exposes protection shortfalls
records.description: Soil microbiomes harbour diverse genetic resources that underpin their capacity to provide crucial ecosystem services (for example, nutrient cycling). Here the authors map global hotspots of soil microbial genetic resources from 1,609 soil metagenomes to inform actionable targets for their protection.

records.title: Subnational mechanisms undermine transnational anti-deforestation policies
records.description: Dry forests, such as the Argentine Chaco, are protected by a mix of local and foreign policies. However, strategies to relax local forest zoning laws circumvent dry forest protection, increasing pressure on foreign policies to move towards zero gross deforestation.

records.title: Psychological barriers to improving carbon competence
records.description: The psychological processes obstructing carbon competence—the acquisition of knowledge about the relative mitigation potential of different actions—are not well known. This study investigates the psychological barriers to developing carbon competence and explores interventions to overcome them.

records.title: From corporate net-zero pledges to credible climate action
records.description: Although corporate net-zero pledges have become popular, evidence suggests they are not having real-world impacts, most probably because they lack a scientific foundation to ensure credibility and integrity. This Perspective presents a scientific framework to address the issue.

records.title: Spiralling frontier threats in Indigenous Amazonia
records.description: Indigenous Lands are critical for protecting Indigenous Peoples and the Amazon. Yet, they are increasingly exposed to socio-environmental frontiers, bringing violence, illegal resource extraction and deforestation. Urgent action is required to prevent irreversible harm to both people and forests, particularly in Brazil’s Vale do Javari Indigenous Land.

records.title: Towards safe and just planetary boundaries for novel entities
records.description: The uncontrolled production and release of human-made substances, or novel entities, has substantial environmental consequences. Here the authors propose a framework for assessing the long-term safety and environmental impacts of these novel entities that accounts for their vast number, diversity and complex interactions.

records.title: Advancing sustainable aquaculture with a zero-valent copper filter system
records.description: Algal blooms severely threaten water safety, but conventional algae elimination methods are chemical-intense. This study presents a zero-valent copper microporous filter capable of removing algal cells and other harmful pollutants from aquaculture water without chemical input.

records.title: Research priorities for addressing global absorbent hygiene product waste
records.description: Absorbent hygiene products (AHPs) — child diapers, adult incontinence products and period products — are a major source of plastic waste. This Perspective highlights the materials and societal complexity of AHP waste and identifies opportunities for scientists to help address the unfolding AHP crisis.

records.title: The politics of measuring sustainability progress and citizen science
records.description: Developing indicators, and the methodologies behind them, should make space for participatory approaches if we are to shape interventions equitably and effectively, argues Dilek Fraisl.

records.title: On the relevance of post-growth in China
records.description: Post-growth debates largely ignore China, despite its key position in the world economy, leaving a gap in sustainability discourse. This Perspective examines China’s role in a post-growth transition, comparing post-growth principles with China’s development model.

records.title: When drought meets war trauma
records.description: The human consequences of armed conflict and climate change are often studied separately despite frequent co-occurrence of those events in fragile regions. A study now reveals a compounding effect of drought on post-traumatic stress from war, underlining the need for mental health services as a component of adaptation and humanitarian responses.
