records.title: On the relevance of post-growth in China
records.description: Post-growth debates largely ignore China, despite its key position in the world economy, leaving a gap in sustainability discourse. This Perspective examines China’s role in a post-growth transition, comparing post-growth principles with China’s development model.

records.title: When drought meets war trauma
records.description: The human consequences of armed conflict and climate change are often studied separately despite frequent co-occurrence of those events in fragile regions. A study now reveals a compounding effect of drought on post-traumatic stress from war, underlining the need for mental health services as a component of adaptation and humanitarian responses.

records.title: Culturalizing sustainability
records.description: Policy-makers and scientists dominate high-level sustainability debates but any decision that follows has consequences for ordinary people in their local communities and environments. We asked experts to reflect on the importance of embracing a culturally informed, bottom-up approach to the sustainability discourse and action.

records.title: Drought amplifies the psychological burden of war
records.description: Integrating georeferenced drought data from respondents’ pre-displacement regions with survey data from Syrian and Iraqi refugees, this study finds a stronger association between war exposure and post-traumatic stress among individuals from more drought-affected areas of origin.

records.title: African water research beyond the narratives of conflict and scarcity
records.description: Reproducible, replicable and robust African water research remains underrepresented in highly visible scientific journals, leading regional policymakers to turn to consulting firms and interest groups. We call for stronger editorial engagement with African water research to leverage its contributions to transboundary conflict resolution.

records.title: The true impacts of the built environment
records.description: Cement and concrete underpin modern societies, yet their true resource demands and the dynamics that govern their efficient use remain poorly understood. Two recent studies suggest that the most powerful levers for change may not lie inside the cement plant at all.

records.title: Recognizing the human health impacts of marine heatwaves
records.description: Although the physical and ecological impacts of marine heatwaves are well recognized, their cascading consequences for human health remain poorly understood. We argue that marine heatwaves pose growing physical and mental health risks that must be treated as a distinct, core climate concern requiring anticipatory action.

records.title: Author Correction: Spatial assessment of tap-water safety in China
Evidence and limits of restitution
records.description: Assessing whether returning land to Indigenous communities delivers on its environmental promise requires evidence that goes beyond titling of continuously occupied lands. A study now uses three decades of satellite data on Mapuche land restitution in Chile to show how restitution reshapes landscapes, but opens space to ask what such evidence can and cannot see.

records.title: Environmental impacts of Indigenous land restitution in Chile
records.description: Indigenous land restitution is often expected to deliver environmental co-benefits alongside redressing historical dispossession, but evidence of land-use change after restitution is limited. This study evaluates the land-use and environmental impacts of returning over 200,000 ha to Mapuche communities in Chile.

records.title: Residents near small rivers in the USA could face disproportionately high future flood risk
records.description: Analysis combining high-resolution hydrodynamic simulations and demographic projections across the contiguous USA suggests that residents near small rivers face a disproportionately higher flood risk by 2050 than those near larger ones. This enhanced flood risk is mainly due to low defence levels and increases in projected flood magnitude under climate change.

records.title: Addressing water resource constraints for electrolytic hydrogen demand in China
records.description: Scaling up electrolytic hydrogen is central to deep decarbonization, but its substantial water needs clash with growing water scarcity. A study mapping 2,853 Chinese county-level cities shows that using reclaimed water can unlock 99% of water-constrained carbon mitigation at only ~20% higher cost.

records.title: Monitoring nature-based solutions is key for compliance, co-creation and practice improvement
records.description: Upholding international environmental commitments calls for monitoring and evaluation practices that bridge international ambitions and local action in cities. This Perspective suggests how to reframe monitoring and evaluation to leverage community involvement to respond to changing conditions.

records.title: Resilience metrics to guide back-up investments in the power system during extreme weather
records.description: Net-zero power systems are vulnerable to extreme weather, but how much back-up capacity is needed to keep systems reliable under variable weather remains unclear. A study using 80 years of European data identifies key stress events and proposes metrics for short- and long-term resilience.

records.title: Human mobility dynamics for cost-effective flood emergency resource allocation
records.description: Flood emergency resources are often misallocated as planning relies on static population data rather than dynamic human mobility during disasters. A study now models flood-induced mobility across 21 Chinese cities, revealing widespread resource mismatches and cost-effective retrofitting strategies.

records.title: Author Correction: Strong and recyclable bio-derived poly(ester amide) hot-melt adhesive
Future flood risk concentration for residents near small rivers across the USA
records.description: Climate change is expected to intensify river flooding, yet small rivers are often overlooked in large-scale risk assessments. A study now projects that residents along small rivers in the USA face the highest future flood risk and the largest defence-investment needs by 2050.

records.title: Urban water affordability crisis exacerbated by climate change
records.description: Water affordability is a growing challenge, but how climate change may worsen it through costly infrastructure adaptation remains unclear. This study models climate-driven water affordability in Santa Cruz, California, finding that climate change alone could double water bills by mid-century.

records.title: Increased dengue transmission following highway paving in the Peruvian Amazon
records.description: Road construction can be crucial in providing economic opportunities, yet how such infrastructure development links to infectious disease transmission is uncertain. This study examines the role of the 2009 highway construction in the Madre de Dios region of Peru on dengue transmission dynamics.

records.title: Decoupling development from concrete
records.description: Enormous consumption of concrete is straining planetary boundaries, yet it remains unclear how to reduce resource burdens while sustaining human development. A study now finds that concrete demand in rapidly developing economies has driven increased resource use over the past three decades, and production improvements have only marginally reduced resource burdens.

records.title: Greater losses from heat exposure experienced by female smallholders in sub-Saharan Africa
records.description: The disproportionate risks of crop damage and food insecurity from temperature anomalies affecting female smallholders are hard to measure. Estimating yield responses to temperature variation across sub-Saharan Africa, this study shows significantly higher losses to female than male smallholders.

records.title: Increasing global threat of outburst floods from overlooked small alpine lakes
records.description: Outburst floods from small alpine lakes pose a growing risk to mountain communities, which are often already marginalized and lack adaptation options. Cryosphere degradation accelerates these threats, adding urgency to integrate small high-mountain lakes into climate and disaster policy.

records.title: Resource consumption in global concrete production
records.description: Concrete production exceeds that of other construction materials, yet the resources required are poorly tracked. This study quantifies the global inputs and hidden losses, revealing that 66 Gt of mineral, energy and water resources were consumed in 2019—more than double previous direct-use estimates.

records.title: Material equality undermined by global trade
records.description: Meeting the increasing demand for water, energy and food of the global population in a just and sustainable manner is an urgent challenge. A study now maps how these essential, interdependent systems are leveraged in international trade, quantifying both physical and virtual flows across countries.

records.title: Dynamic solvent exchange for fast-charging lithium batteries and beyond
records.description: This work identifies dynamic solvent exchange as the governing kinetic descriptor for desolvation, enabling a dual-anion electrolyte design that overcomes traditional trade-offs to achieve fast-charging, all-climate battery performance.

records.title: Respiratory-inspired electrostatic open-microfluidics for air purification
records.description: Efficient air purification is essential to improve air quality and safeguard human health. Inspired by the human respiratory system, the authors develop an electrostatic open-microfluidics air filter system for the efficient removal of airborne pollutants.

records.title: Demand-side factors as dominant drivers of resource efficiency in the concrete aggregates cycle
records.description: Cement, concrete and aggregates dominate global resource use, but it is unclear whether future efficiency gains will come mainly from production- or demand-side changes. A study now analyses the concrete aggregates cycle across 184 economies, showing that demand-side drivers dominate efficiency changes.

records.title: Sustainable all-silk textiles for personal thermal management
records.description: Traditional synthetic textiles for radiative cooling often rely on additives that risk releasing harmful microplastics and toxic nanoparticles. This work shows an all-silk nanotextile that achieves superior personal thermal management while ensuring full biodegradability and a minimal environmental footprint.

records.title: Synergistic pathways to mitigate climate and water scarcity risks
records.description: Combining carbon capture and storage (CCS) with enhanced water recovery could be a viable solution to improve the sustainability of the energy–carbon–water system. With a high-resolution CCS source–sink matching model for coal-fired power plants, this study analyses this synergistic approach in China.

records.title: A versatile sustainable biosubstrate stabilizing metal conductors for soft sensors
records.description: The growing market for soft electronics largely relies on fossil fuel-based polymer substrates. This work points towards a more sustainable future for the field by presenting a bio-based substrate for metal-on-polymer soft sensors that are degradable, recyclable, interfacially robust, mechanically tough and self-reparable.

records.title: Broad-spectrum insecticide detoxification for the protection of managed pollinators
records.description: Pollination services are crucial for crop cultivation worldwide but pollinators face detrimental effects from insecticide exposure. Here, the authors develop a broad-spectrum insecticide detoxification technology that has the potential to protect managed pollinators such as bumblebees.

records.title: Author Correction: Effects of forestry decentralization on rural inequality in Nepal
Limited reach of zero-deforestation commitments to Indonesian oil palm smallholders
records.description: Zero-deforestation commitments in the Indonesian palm oil sector have limited reach among smallholders. This study combines surveys and interviews to assess market access and deforestation, finding limited smallholder inclusion and minimal differences in forest outcomes.

records.title: Neighbourhood design and the environmental and social costs of suburbanization
records.description: The growth of suburban areas increases car use, raises emissions and affects social cohesion, but it is unclear whether this is driven by suburban design or distance from the city centre. This study estimates the social and environmental effects of the garden city design concept on neighbourhoods in the USA.

records.title: Human health effects of amine-based carbon capture and storage in the US electricity sector
records.description: Postcombustion carbon capture and storage (CCS) at power plants can lower CO 2 emissions, but the health benefits may depend on the solvents used and control of related NH 3 emissions. The authors assess the climate and health impacts of CCS adoption at coal and natural gas combined cycle power plants in the USA.

records.title: Association of mortality and combined oxidative capacity of ozone and nitrogen dioxide
records.description: Ozone and nitrogen dioxide are air pollutants linked to adverse health outcomes, yet the impacts of their combined oxidative capacity across multiple regions are unclear. The authors assess the association between the combined oxidative capacity of ozone and nitrogen dioxide and daily mortality for 380 cities.

records.title: Rooftop photovoltaic-powered electric vehicle charging for accelerated decarbonization
records.description: Matching rooftop solar output with electric vehicle charging demand remains a barrier to scaling solar-powered transport. A study now evaluates this across 40 global cities, showing that solar generation can meet the demand projected for 2050 with substantial economic and decarbonization benefits.

records.title: Author Correction: Global expansion of the ecological impact of extra-urban road traffic
Sustainable battery recycling through spatial and technological alignment
records.description: Battery recycling has a crucial role in enabling circular economy and sustainable energy transition. This study presents a multi-scale analytical framework to assist the design of low-carbon, high-efficiency battery recycling systems.

records.title: Rooftop photovoltaic-powered electric vehicle charging for accelerated decarbonization
records.description: Matching rooftop solar output with electric vehicle charging demand remains a barrier to scaling solar-powered transport. A study now evaluates this across 40 global cities, showing that solar generation can meet the demand projected for 2050 with substantial economic and decarbonization benefits.

records.title: Author Correction: Global expansion of the ecological impact of extra-urban road traffic
Sustainable battery recycling through spatial and technological alignment
records.description: Battery recycling has a crucial role in enabling circular economy and sustainable energy transition. This study presents a multi-scale analytical framework to assist the design of low-carbon, high-efficiency battery recycling systems.

records.title: Uniting forces for green carbon chemicals
records.description: The shift towards renewable carbon for producing everyday chemicals hinges on innovative strategies to utilize sustainable feedstocks. By synergizing catalysis and reaction engineering, scientists can now incorporate renewable fatty acids into high-value end products, enhancing the potential of a circular bioeconomy.

records.title: Forcing self-metathesis reaction beyond thermodynamic equilibrium for green chemicals
records.description: The self-cross metathesis of oleic acid esters enables synthesis of valuable, fully biosourced chemicals, but its productivity is thermodynamically limited to 50%. Here the authors overcome this limit to double the reaction yield by using a reactive distillation set-up.

records.title: Global patterns of reservoir sedimentation and overlooked risks in small reservoirs
records.description: Global reservoirs are under threat from increasing sedimentation rates, which threaten infrastructure function and storage capacity. A focus on large reservoirs underestimates the scale of the problem and the importance of resilient small reservoirs for global water security.

records.title: Energy-efficient electrified ethylene synthesis in CO-starved environment
records.description: Electrochemical carbon monoxide (CO) reduction offers a viable approach to sustainable ethylene production, but remains challenging under low CO availability. This study shows how to achieve efficient and selective ethylene synthesis in a CO-starved environment.

records.title: A circular hydrothermal refinery for sustainable aviation fuel from food waste
records.description: Decarbonizing aviation is critical for global sustainability. The authors show a circular hydrothermal refinery transforming food waste into a 100% drop-in sustainable aviation fuel rich in cycloalkanes.

records.title: Bird migration and wind-energy production across Western Europe
records.description: Renewable wind energy can aid decarbonization efforts; however, the impacts of wind turbines on migrating birds remain unclear. The authors study the potential risks of wind energy installations on migrating bird populations across Western Europe and assess potential trade-offs between wind energy and conservation.

records.title: The stability–activity tension in metal–organic framework catalysis
records.description: As materials with highly versatile and tunable architectures and functionalities, metal–organic frameworks offer precise control over catalyst structures. We discuss how their sustainable and economically viable use depends on balancing activity, stability and scale through improved metrics and informed material design.

records.title: Farming needs more hands
records.description: Climate change may shift where crops can grow, but it will not determine who farms the land. A modelling study suggests that shrinking agricultural workforces could leave climatically suitable large areas practically unavailable for cultivation.

records.title: Agricultural workforce as a potential bottleneck of future cropland availability
records.description: Future food demand is expected to drive cropland expansion, but emerging agricultural workforce shortages, contributing to local cropland abandonment, might limit food production. This study models the future impacts of labour constraints on cropland use under socioeconomic and climate scenarios.

records.title: Upgrading glycerol to sorbose via a tandem photoelectrocatalysis–enzyme catalysis relay
records.description: As a low-cost by-product of biodiesel production, glycerol is an attractive feedstock for the sustainable manufacturing of high-value chemicals. This study demonstrates a method to convert glycerol into sorbose, a valuable sugar used in the food and pharmaceutical industries.

records.title: Driving a green energy transition with halide perovskite solar cells
records.description: This Review shifts the focus of research on perovskite solar cells from efficiency to industrial reliability, scalability and circularity, providing a strategic roadmap for sustainable manufacturing by analysing life-cycle impacts and fail-safe scaling strategies.

records.title: Widespread range contraction of carnivores in protected areas of China
records.description: Protected areas can be important in conserving key mammal species that help maintain ecosystem functioning. The authors examine how well protected areas achieve this, in the context of historical habitat loss and human–wildlife conflict, for 82 mammal species across China.

records.title: Upcycling of plastic garbage bags to graphene@silica fabric for sensing platforms
records.description: Most flexible sensors are fabricated using polymer-based substrates, which are intrinsically unsustainable and insufficiently robust. This study shows a strategy for using waste plastic to fabricate graphene-based flexible sensors that can address the drawbacks of polymer-based sensors.

records.title: The long environmental shadow of war
records.description: Fuel and water infrastructure are increasingly becoming the targets of military conflicts. These attacks pose not only a direct threat to civilian health and safety, but an ongoing threat to the environment that may persist for decades. Military strikes on civilian-critical infrastructure must be condemned if we are to build a just and sustainable future.

records.title: A multidimensional assessment of systemic cooling poverty in the global south
records.description: The multiple factors preventing people from staying safe during heatwaves and hot spells are poorly quantified. A study now measures systemic cooling poverty in the global south, revealing that almost 600 million people are at risk of heat-related harm and that deprivation patterns vary markedly both across and within countries.

records.title: Improved forest protection at Chinese heritage relic sites
records.description: Deforestation over the past century represents a crucial challenge for biodiversity conservation, but whether biocultural sites can improve conservation outcomes is still unclear. This study examines biocultural sites across China to test how these influence forest conservation outcomes.

records.title: Towards sustainable metal–organic frameworks from lab to practice
records.description: Realistic life-cycle impacts of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are rarely quantified, despite their promise for carbon capture, water treatment, catalysis and other environmental applications. Here we propose a compact, actionable sustainability toolkit for MOFs to systematically verify claims of ‘green’.

records.title: Synergies between poverty reduction and biodiversity conservation
records.description: Greater household dependence on forest resources is associated with lower tree species diversity in tropical forests, highlighting the interconnected dynamics of poverty and biodiversity in multifunctional landscapes. Forest policies that aim to conserve biodiversity must consider the interconnected dynamics of poverty alleviation and biodiversity conservation to achieve multiple sustainability goals.

records.title: Advancing biodiversity through poverty solutions
records.description: Forest biodiversity is linked, in many cases, to the myriad ecosystem services that support the livelihoods of human populations. Authors here examine the demographic, socioeconomic and institutional variables that impact forest biodiversity across 322 tropical forests.

records.title: Sea-level-driven land conversion amplified by coastal agriculture
records.description: As sea levels rise, coastal ecosystems and economies are threatened by saltwater intrusion and wetland encroachment. These effects are accelerated by coastal agriculture, highlighting the importance of local management interventions.

records.title: Coal plants persist as a large barrier to the global solar energy transition
records.description: Solar power is critical to the energy transition, but aerosols emitted from co-located coal plants suppress solar power production, diminishing realized energy gains. Although stricter emissions controls can partially mitigate these effects, a phase-out of coal-fired power would more effectively remove this performance constraint.

records.title: Enduring cultural legacies affect Euro-American wildlife values
records.description: Little is known about how values emerge, evolve and affect people’s relation with their natural environment. A study now sheds light on the influence of the institutions of European colonization on present-day values towards wildlife in the Americas.

records.title: Best practices for thermoelectric materials and devices
records.description: Thermoelectric technology offers a robust solid-state solution for energy harvesting and thermal management, but fragmented measurement standards and a disconnect between materials discovery and device engineering stymie both rigorous benchmarking and commercial translation. Here, we identify common drawbacks and suggest how to harmonize evaluation.

records.title: A solvent-free route to high-performance silk materials
records.description: The fabrication of silk materials typically requires large amounts of solvents. Now, a simple thermomechanical strategy enables natural silk fibres to be directly fused into strong, multifunctional materials without solution processing. By preserving silk’s hierarchical structure, this approach, which is amenable to scale-up, offers a sustainable route towards high-performance bio-derived materials.

records.title: Hierarchical materials from fused silk
records.description: Natural silk, mechanically strong and biodegradable, offers great potential for sustainable functional materials. Here the authors present a simple thermomechanical method for fabricating high-performance structural and optically active materials directly from silk fibres.

records.title: 3D-printed multiscale-ordered hierarchical frameworks for rapid atmospheric water harvesting
records.description: Atmospheric water harvesting provides a vital pathway for mitigating freshwater scarcity. This study introduces a 3D-printed porous structure designed for rapid water capture, overcoming a critical bottleneck that has long hindered the large-scale deployment of atmospheric water harvesting technology.

records.title: Sweet spots for nitrogen reduction in a coastal watershed
records.description: Coastal nitrogen pollution is a critical sustainability challenge with environmental, social and economic consequences. Upstream ‘sweet spots’ where interventions will have maximum mitigation effectiveness and social buy-in are attractive but may prove difficult to implement in urban stream networks.

records.title: Evaluative governance for climate action in Australia
records.description: National climate risk frameworks catalogue threats but rarely define which risks are tolerable, to whom and how to decide. We propose embedding evaluative governance — the structures, processes and relationships that guide law, policy, deliberation, funding and evaluation — across the policy cycle to translate into accountable, equitable and adaptive climate action.

records.title: Rebirth of phosphorus in wastewater
records.description: For decades, phosphorus recovery from wastewater has largely relied on organic carbon supplementation, which affects the sustainability of the recovery process. Research has now found a methanotrophic polyphosphate-accumulating organism capable of low-carbon phosphorus recovery.

records.title: Rice–fish co-culturing reduces schistosomiasis risk and increases yields and incomes
records.description: Rice is a staple food for many households; however, its cultivation can expose farming families to parasitic diseases such as schistosomiasis via freshwater snails. The authors examine how integrating native fish into rice fields can suppress snail hosts, boost yields and improve farmer livelihoods.

records.title: Low-temperature polyethylene terephthalate upcycling by phenolic ionic liquids
records.description: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) upcycling is desired to achieve a circular economy but hindered by harsh operation conditions and the need for costly down-processing. Here the authors develop a low-temperature PET upcycling strategy that is capable of directly delivering valuable final products.

records.title: Methanotroph-driven phosphorus recovery for sustainable wastewater management
records.description: Low-carbon biological phosphorus recovery is indispensable for achieving sustainable wastewater management but remains challenging. This work discovers a methanotrophic polyphosphate-accumulating organism and demonstrates its potential in low-carbon phosphorus recovery.

records.title: Water scarcity and infrastructure risk of amplified seasonal sediment transport
records.description: The changing seasonality of river runoff and sediment in mountain regions concerns water managers as warmer, wetter conditions degrade the cryosphere. Extreme seasonal sediment transport has resulted in river mobility that threatens regional agriculture and infrastructure.

records.title: Pulsed bubble-induced ultrahigh electrostatic potentials for triboelectric air purification
records.description: Purifying air contaminated with particulate matter is crucial to improve air quality. Here the authors introduce a triboelectric air filter that leverages pulsed bubble-induced electrostatic potentials to realize the efficient removal of particulate matter from air.

records.title: Harnessing legal system complexity for radical shifts to sustainability
records.description: Legal systems can either enable or constrain shifts to sustainability. Here the authors bridge computational network analysis with qualitative legal expertise to develop a conceptual framework that can help identify and target changes to existing laws that can trigger system-wide effects.

records.title: Climate-driven depopulation and adaptation realities in America’s coastal ground zero
records.description: Climate change-induced sea-level rise poses a significant societal challenge, but the extent of potential inundation remains uncertain. Looking at the recent geologic past and at prehistoric human adaptation provides valuable insights into possible new coastlines and strategies to help inform the future of modern coastal communities.

records.title: Upcycling plant biomass into photosynthetic microspheres for diabetic wound healing
records.description: This study showcases the upcycling of invasive water hyacinth into photosynthetic microspheres which provide sustained oxygen evolution and metabolic regulation, significantly accelerating the healing process of chronic diabetic wounds.

records.title: Solar-spectral electrochromic glazing using suspended clusters in an organogel
records.description: Creating scalable and cost-effective smart windows that modulate solar radiation has long been a challenge. A simple electrochromic organogel can effectively tune solar radiation entering indoor space through the dynamic aggregation of polyoxometalate clusters, enabling large-area, low-cost glazing for energy-efficient buildings and vehicles.

records.title: Methane leakage can erase the climate benefits of wastewater biogas recovery
records.description: Wastewater utilities use anaerobic digestion and biogas utilization to reduce energy costs and emissions, but methane leakage can undermine both the climate benefits and project economics of these systems, especially as power grids decarbonize. Safeguarding climate integrity will require performance-based methane policies that pair robust monitoring with enforceable leakage thresholds and targeted leak detection and repair.

records.title: Positive tipping points for nature
records.description: Enacting the social and environmental change needed to address the most pressing sustainability challenges can prove unwieldy. However, identifying positive tipping points that accelerate positive feedback cycles may be the key to large-scale natural recovery.

records.title: Methane leakage thresholds for net climate benefits of wastewater biogas recovery
records.description: Biogas recovery enables renewable energy production alongside waste treatment, but the climate benefits are compromised by methane leakage. Here the authors systematically assessed how to manage methane leakage for sustaining net climate benefits of wastewater biogas recovery.

records.title: Scalable all-in-one electrochromic glazing for full-spectrum solar radiation management
records.description: Electrochromic windows provide an energy-efficient pathway to manage thermal efficiency. This work describes a glazing design that is scalable, stable over cycling and functional for a wide solar spectrum.

records.title: Filament-catalyst lightbulb reactor for efficient methane conversion
records.description: Direct non-oxidative conversion of methane into valuable hydrocarbons is a highly promising low-carbon pathway. This study presents a filament-catalyst reactor that spatially separates high-temperature methane activation from low-temperature product formation for better efficiency and selectivity.

records.title: Turning the tide of climate solutions to save tidal flats
records.description: Tidal flats are vital carbon sinks and biodiversity hotspots, yet they face increasing threats from misapplied climate solutions, including mangrove afforestation and renewable energy expansion. Protecting tidal flats from well-intentioned but misapplied solutions is crucial for aligning global climate and biodiversity goals.

records.title: Decades of increased emissions from forest-fuelled BECCS
records.description: Governments are considering subsidies for bioenergy with carbon capture and storage fuelled by wood from existing forests. However, a transparent model estimates that this will probably increase emissions for decades, increase electricity costs 3.5-fold and not generate negative emissions for 150 years.

records.title: Scalable synthesis of graphitic aggregates for high-rate battery anode
records.description: This work shows a sustainable, scalable and cost-effective synthetic process from polyacrylonitrile precursors for the production of high-performance carbon anode in lithium-ion batteries.

records.title: Methane pyrolysis-enabled production of high-value carbon fibres
records.description: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas, but can also be used as a source for advanced carbon materials. This work shows a sustainable approach to produce high-value carbon fibres through methane pyrolysis.

records.title: The linkage between microbial community dynamics and urbanization age
records.description: Urbanization can affect the dynamics of microbial communities, which can, in turn, have implications for public health. By leveraging global metagenome datasets, the authors study the impact of urbanization age on microbial communities for actionable insights for urban planning and public health.

records.title: Realizing an equitable circular bionutrient economy in the United States
records.description: Most crop-producing regions in the USA experience critical organic nutrient deficits. These deficits could be addressed by the coordinated local reuse of important nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus sourced from human and livestock waste.

records.title: Ubiquitous mobility data enable near-real-time emission estimates for urban traffic
records.description: Ubiquitous mobility data from traffic cameras and mobile phones enable large-scale, fine-grained, near-real-time estimation of traffic emissions. Our analysis reveals systematic biases in conventional urban emission inventories and shows that Manhattan’s congestion pricing programme led to a 16–22% reduction in traffic emissions in the 8 weeks after its implementation.

records.title: Electrifying water treatment at device level
records.description: Electrochemical processes enable the efficient removal of persistent water pollutants, yet real-world applications are hindered by electrolyte addition and low overall energy efficiency. A device design now addresses these challenges, enabling electrolyte-free operation while coupling cathodic and anodic processes to improve treatment and energy efficiencies.

records.title: Solar-driven biosynthesis of chemicals from phosphite-rich wastewater and carbon dioxide
records.description: Bio-photosynthesis has the potential to achieve sustainable chemical production, but technical challenges remain. This work proposes a solar–chemical hybrid-driven biosynthesis strategy to achieve efficient chemical production from wastewater and carbon dioxide.

records.title: A sustainable transition to electric minibus taxis in Cape Town’s paratransit
records.description: Paratransit dominates mobility in sub-Saharan Africa, yet electrification of the sector is rarely discussed. A study on Cape Town’s minibus taxis now finds that electrification is feasible with depot and home charging, and discusses the implications in terms of grid demand, air quality and equity issues.

records.title: The dual impact of trade on the water–energy–food nexus globally
records.description: Global trade tightly links water, energy and food systems, but its effects on cross-border sustainability and equity remain unclear. A study now maps global water–energy–food trade networks, finding that trade balances overall resource gains while deepening cross-country income inequalities.

records.title: Ubiquitous data-driven framework for traffic emission estimation and policy evaluation
records.description: Urban traffic emission estimates are often too coarse or slow to evaluate decarbonization policies. A study now fuses data from traffic cameras and mobile phones to estimate citywide emissions in near-real time, finding strong spatiotemporal variation and a 16–22% emission drop after congestion pricing.

records.title: Liquid droplet mops
records.description: Surface cleaning is needed in various industrial systems but remains water intensive due to low water utilization efficiency. This study proposes a method—liquid droplet mops—that can efficiently clean superhydrophobic-coated solar panels with substantially reduced water consumption.

records.title: Scalable flow-through device for electrochemical water treatment without secondary pollution
records.description: Electrochemical advanced oxidation water treatment processes (EAOPs) can help achieve a sustainable water cycle but remain challenging to scale up and implement. This study presents a flow-through EAOP device design that features good scalability and exhibits high practical application potential.

records.title: Global copper tailings distribution and projection
records.description: Copper is a critical resource for the energy transition, but the associated mine waste and tailings present an environmental hazard. Global copper tailings generation is projected to continue to rise until at least the middle of the century, prompting a need for a coordinated, multilateral strategy to manage copper mine tailings.

records.title: Spatially coupled adsorption and catalysis for sustainable lithium–sulfur batteries
records.description: Although lithium–sulfur batteries are prized for their sustainability, practical energy densities are often limited by heavy host materials. The authors report a graphdiyne architecture that integrates anchoring and catalytic functions, enabling ultrahigh sulfur loading and exceptional energy densities, even in pouch-cell configuration.

records.title: Fire dynamics in the South American Chaco and their link to agriculture and drought
records.description: Climate change, particularly intensifying droughts, is often blamed for wildfires across the Gran Chaco, a vast South American dry woodland. An analysis of over 30 years of fire patterns, however, reveals that the majority of fires are driven by agricultural expansion and deforestation.

records.title: Challenges and opportunities for the governance of hydropower
records.description: Massive hydropower expansion in the global south repeats unsustainable past social and environmental harms, raising questions about how to govern these projects effectively. This Review highlights shifting and evolving global dynamics, and identifies opportunities for more just and strategic hydropower governance.

records.title: Towards glues that won’t stick around
records.description: Adhesives conveniently hold together a wide variety of physical objects, but they carry an underappreciated environmental burden. More sustainable alternatives are urgently needed.

records.title: The invisible sustainability problem of glues and how to solve it
records.description: Adhesives are hard to see when in use, but they force most products to reside in landfills for centuries. Ongoing research is creating opportunities in materials design and market impact, thereby helping society move towards a more sustainable future.

records.title: Strong and recyclable bio-derived poly(ester amide) hot-melt adhesive
records.description: Petroleum-based adhesives are used ubiquitously in daily life and therefore contribute to persistent waste generation. Here the authors synthesize a robust and strong poly(ester amide) adhesive that can be derived from biomass feedstocks and chemically recycled at the end of its life.

records.title: Photovoltaics for food security
records.description: Besides decarbonizing energy supply, photovoltaics can also largely enhance the resilience of global food supply, argues Zhenguo Li.

records.title: Optimizing biodiversity, multifunctionality and yield when transitioning to organic farming
records.description: Different agricultural management systems, for example, conventional versus organic, can have different benefits and challenges. Authors here examine the biodiversity, crop yield and ecosystem multifunctionality impacts of transitioning from conventional to organic agriculture across 179 global croplands.

records.title: Microbial upcycling of plastic waste to levodopa
records.description: The production of high-value chemicals can involve energy-intensive processes, necessitating sustainable production strategies. Here the authors present a circular bioeconomy approach, upcycling plastic waste through microbial conversion into levodopa, a medicine for Parkinson’s disease.

records.title: Iran’s policy priorities intensify water crisis
records.description: The chronic water crisis in Iran stems from decades of water-intensive development, fragmented governance and national priorities that sidelined environmental protection. Without major governance reform and reprioritization, technical solutions alone cannot stop worsening water and environmental degradation.

records.title: Sleep loss in a warming world
records.description: High temperatures disrupt sleep worldwide, with disproportionate impacts on older adults, women and populations in lower-income countries. A study uses climate change simulations to project future global sleep erosion and, in turn, the decline in childhood general cognitive ability and associated socioeconomic costs.

records.title: Effect of climate-driven childhood sleep erosion on potential regional economic inequality
records.description: Hot climates erode children’s sleep, threatening cognitive development with likely socioeconomic consequences. A global analysis finds potential links between future sleep losses and trillions of dollars in economic costs that disproportionately burden poorer regions.

records.title: Rewiring energy flow in biohybrids for enhanced solar-driven biosynthesis
records.description: Solar-driven biosynthesis using semiconductor biohybrids has the potential to achieve sustainable chemical production, but often it is hindered by inefficient solar energy conversion. Here the authors develop design strategies to tackle this technical challenge.

records.title: Compostable soft robots for plant monitoring
records.description: Soft robots inspired by living organisms hold the promise of gentle, adaptable interactions with the natural world, but leave behind persistent waste. Now scientists show a fully compostable robotic system that addresses this limitation by offering durable performance and decomposing safely into the soil at the end of its life.

records.title: Nuclear fuel from saline waters
records.description: Growing demand for nuclear fuel is accelerating the need for sustainable uranium resources that ensure long-term supply and mitigate environmental risks. A study now presents an intriguing self-powered methodology that utilizes the motion of falling water droplets to drive uranium recovery from salt lakes.

records.title: Spontaneous uranium extraction from salt-lake water via droplet falling
records.description: More environmentally friendly methods of extracting uranium from alternative sources are needed for the sustainable development of the nuclear power industry. This work proposes a spontaneous extraction process driven by droplet falling that enables the extraction of uranium from salt lakes.

records.title: Biodegradable yet hyperdurable robotic fingers for zero-waste soft electronics
records.description: As soft electronic waste becomes an urgent concern, biodegradable yet high-performance devices are emerging as a promising solution. Here the authors fabricate durable and multifunctional soft robotic fingers in which both polymers and inorganic electronics are fully compostable.

records.title: A programmable microbial assembly line for plastic upcycling
records.description: Strategies to upcycle plastic waste are critically needed to mitigate their impacts on the environment and public health. Here the authors introduce a programmable, microbial-based platform that converts end-of-life plastics into a suite of high-value products, ranging from fuels to biopolymers.

records.title: Actions and actors driving transformative change for global sustainability
records.description: A bibliometric analysis of more than four million scholarly documents highlights the need for a more inclusive approach to research on actors and actions needed for transformative change towards a just and sustainable world and more emphasis on the synergies between actors and actions that drive change.

records.title: Multi-zonal anaerobic ammonium oxidation for mainstream municipal wastewater treatment
records.description: Anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox) has great potential in sustainable wastewater treatment, but its implementation in mainstream wastewater treatment is challenging. This work proposes a ‘multi-zonal anammox’ concept that can be incorporated into existing wastewater treatment plants.

records.title: Catalytic bromine recycling from waste
records.description: Bromine (Br) has indispensable roles in manufacturing many products but mostly ends up in waste, leading to both resource loss and environmental pollution. Here the authors proposes a catalytic process to enable Br recycling from real-world Br-laden wastes.

records.title: A water-soluble binder for recyclable lithium-ion batteries
records.description: The growing volume of end-of-life batteries calls for circular economy solutions. This work presents a water-soluble binder that enables the fast separation of active materials from current collectors in aqueous solutions for sustainable recycling of electrode materials.

records.title: Solution-processed electrochromics for synergistic solar and radiative heat management
records.description: The severity of climate change impacts calls for low-carbon thermal management solutions. This work presents a chameleon-inspired electronic skin for adaptive electrochromic thermal regulation with minimal energy input and scalability potential.

records.title: Electrolysis with built-in seawater desalination by porous-solid-electrolyte reactor
records.description: Taking advantage of the abundant renewable energy sources along seashores, this work describes a three-chamber electrolyser that combines electrolysis and desalination to produce both freshwater and green hydrogen.

records.title: Ensuring consistency between biogeochemical planetary boundaries
records.description: The planetary boundaries framework has emerged as a powerful tool for assessing the sustainable habitability of our planet. Reassessing these boundaries from a flow-based perspective demonstrates the critical threat posed by climate change relative to other biogeochemical risks.

records.title: Resource requirements and consequences of large-scale hydrogen use in Europe
records.description: Europe’s shift to low-carbon fuels raises concerns about water, land and energy pressures from large-scale hydrogen use. A study now finds that future hydrogen production could overlap with resource and infrastructure constraints, with consequences for the success of a sustainable transition.

records.title: Electrosynthesis of ethylene from syngas
records.description: Producing valuable hydrocarbons electrochemically from carbon monoxide (CO) is an energy-efficient pathway, but reliance on costly pure CO as a feedstock limits its economic viability. This article shows that abundant CO-rich syngas can be directly used to synthesize ethylene.

records.title: Intelligent fouling monitoring in membrane-based wastewater treatment
records.description: Membrane bioreactors play a pivotal role in protecting the water environment and achieving a sustainable urban water cycle, but their operational stability faces great challenges due to membrane fouling. A study now provides an intelligent strategy to enable early warning of fouling events.

records.title: The roles of women in cookstove intervention studies
records.description: This systematic review explores the gender dimensions of cookstove randomized control trials in low- and middle-income countries, published between 2000 and 2024, and highlights the importance of shifting towards more gender-sensitive research designs.

records.title: Pretreating spent lithium-ion batteries
records.description: Reusing materials from spent lithium-ion batteries is a key strategy for developing a sustainable supply chain, but we need to deepen our understanding of the associated environmental impacts. Now, a model-based analysis shows that pretreating end-of-life batteries is critical for enhancing the sustainability of recycling.

records.title: Blue carbon ecosystems and coral reefs as coupled nature-based climate solutions
records.description: Coral reefs are at a planetary tipping point, widely threatened by ocean acidification. Preserving and promoting coastal ecosystems can align with existing nature-based solutions to bolster blue carbon reservoirs to increase ocean alkalinity and support coral reef restoration.

records.title: Impacts of pretreatment routes on spent lithium-ion batteries recycling
records.description: Pretreatment is a prerequisite to recycle spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and advance resource circularity, but its impacts on the overall performance and environmental footprint of LIBs recycling are poorly understood. This study develops unit-level models to address this knowledge gap.

records.title: Race out to eco-friendly peptide synthesis
records.description: The growing demand for therapeutic peptides has intensified concerns about the sustainability of current synthetic processes, which typically rely on excess reagents and, most critically, large volumes of solvents. In the pursuit of more sustainable practices, scientists now report a water-based synthetic protocol.

records.title: Water-based coupling of amino acids for sustainable solid-phase peptide synthesis
records.description: The growing market demand for peptides is drawing more attention to their industrial synthetic procedures, which rely on large amounts of toxic solvents. Here the authors suggest practical steps that bring fully water-based peptide synthesis closer to reality.

records.title: Technology flexibility and sobriety to address shortage of energy-transition metals
records.description: Metals shortage threatens climate goals by affecting adoption of key technologies for the energy transition. Optimizing technology mixes is now shown to limit the supply-constrained energy transition metals to only copper, lithium, and vanadium, though economy-wide resource sobriety remains urgent.

records.title: One Health synergies
records.description: Linking humans, animals, plants, environments and ecosystems to forge healthier lives on a healthier planet clearly aligns with sustainability objectives. A collection of research and opinion presents ideas on the way forward to support such alignment.

records.title: Global evidence synthesis on land-use change and zoonotic risks
records.description: Land-use change, among other anthropogenic factors, has led to increased levels of zoonotic disease transmission. The authors assess how land-use change and restoration activities impact zoonotic disease transmission, providing an online tool useful for One Health-oriented restoration planning.

records.title: Towards One Health action for addressing antimicrobial resistance in the age of polycrisis
records.description: Antimicrobial resistance continues to be a critical One Health challenge, despite research and policy progress. Building on the past decade of research, this Perspective provides an integrative roadmap for addressing antimicrobial resistance by leveraging the complexities of human and environment interactions.

records.title: Livestock antimicrobial use embodied in global supply chains
records.description: Excessive antimicrobial use can increase the threat of antimicrobial resistance; however, how such use is embedded in global trade is still unclear. Authors here estimate global livestock antimicrobial footprints through global supply chains to better understand and manage antimicrobial use.

records.title: Livestock antimicrobial use embodied in global supply chains
records.description: Excessive antimicrobial use can increase the threat of antimicrobial resistance; however, how such use is embedded in global trade is still unclear. Authors here estimate global livestock antimicrobial footprints through global supply chains to better understand and manage antimicrobial use.

records.title: Macroecological approaches for the prediction of zoonotic disease risk
records.description: In recent decades, zoonotic disease outbreaks have become increasingly frequent, necessitating strategies to improve the accuracy of predictive modelling. This Review discusses the importance of macroecological variables in such modelling efforts to improve preparedness for future potential outbreaks.

records.title: A field‑deployable CRISPR-based biosensing platform for monitoring marine ecosystems
records.description: Human impacts on marine ecosystems are increasing the likelihood of pathogenic outbreaks, harmful algal blooms and coral stress. Here the authors develop a CRISPR biomonitoring tool that can help detect key marine species that are important to public health, the aquaculture sector and marine ecosystems.

records.title: Integrating materials innovation and policy challenges for leather alternatives
records.description: The leather industry is at a pivotal moment on its path towards sustainability. Although many bio-based leather alternatives can reduce environmental impact, we need clear definitions of such alternatives to guide materials innovations that truly bring them into the mainstream, sustainable market, as highlighted in a recent court ruling.

records.title: Global gridded dataset of heating and cooling degree days under climate change scenarios
records.description: Accurate projections of heating and cooling needs are vital for planning energy use and achieving the sustainable development goals. A global dataset now maps global heating and cooling degree days, finding future hotspots, rising cooling demand and early shifts in energy needs with major global impacts.

records.title: Levers for equitable material use
records.description: Global household material use is highly unequal: the top 10% drive roughly a third of footprints and most of the overshoot beyond safe limits. Curbing affluent overconsumption, while securing decent material floors, should be a central policy lever to cut material demand quickly and fairly.

records.title: Consumption inequalities in material use undermining resources sustainability
records.description: Global material use is rising unsustainably, but its distribution across individuals remains unclear. A study now reveals deep inequality in household material footprints, especially for non-renewable resources, and suggests that curbing overconsumption among the wealthy is key to sustainability.

records.title: Biochar boom-and-bust cycle
Safeguarding, strengthening and expanding river protections for nature and people
records.description: River protection in the United States remains scant, with just over one-tenth of river length in the contiguous states protected at viable levels, often by land-based protection measures that fail to capture the full diversity of the nation’s river systems. There is an urgent need for policies that safeguard, strengthen and expand freshwater protections to secure rivers that sustain both people and nature.

records.title: Global habitat hotspots and extinction vulnerability of terrestrial vertebrates
records.description: The threat of species extinction is a major problem resulting from various anthropogenic pressures. Here the authors use deep learning models and ecological network theory to study the impacts of human pressures on terrestrial vertebrate habitat hotspots now and under future scenarios of global change.

records.title: National assessment of river protection in the United States
records.description: Although river protection is core to social and environmental well-being, the extent to which river conservation policies are effective is difficult to assess. This study reveals that, under all relevant protection mechanisms in the contiguous USA, only 12% of rivers are adequately protected.

records.title: Meta-analytical evidence of a self–other discrepancy in climate change-related risk perceptions
records.description: People tend to perceive their personal risk from climate change as lower than the risk faced by others, which can demotivate engaging in mitigation actions. A meta-analysis now quantifies this perception gap, showing that its global and regional variation depends on who the ‘other’ is.

records.title: Energy-efficient indirect (bi)carbonate electroreduction in a porous solid electrolyte reactor
records.description: Reactive carbon capture enables CO 2 conversion into valuable chemicals without the typically separate energy-intensive CO 2 recovery step. In this work, the authors suggest minimizing its performance trade-offs via indirect bicarbonate conversion within a porous solid electrolyte reactor.

records.title: Fast and selective CO 2 capture from outdoor air by covalent organic frameworks
records.description: Direct air capture is a promising technology to mitigate the rising atmospheric CO 2 concentrations contributing to climate change. Here a covalent organic framework with high CO 2 capacity and cycling stability is reported to be capable of selectively and rapidly removing CO 2 from open air.

records.title: Climate change-driven contaminants in water
records.description: Climate change creates multiple pathways of water contamination. Here we call for defining climate change-driven contaminants as a distinct class and explore their implications.

records.title: Social factors shape federal environmental crime prosecution patterns in the USA
records.description: This study analyses the geographic patterns of US federal environmental crime prosecutions over 2011–2020, showing that, on average, they tend to occur more in counties with higher socioeconomic status than in the most environmentally degraded areas of the USA.

records.title: Cross-system cascades as drivers of the electrification pathway in net-zero transitions
records.description: Positive cross-system cascades in sustainability transitions are underexplored, despite their potential to accelerate net-zero pathways. This Perspective analyses such cascades in the context of electrification, identifying 12 mechanisms across sociotechnical systems and offering policy recommendations to amplify their impact.

records.title: Unravelling the threads of microfibre terminology
records.description: Although researchers try to understand the physical and chemical impacts of fibre-shaped microscopic pollution, use of inconsistent terminology hinders collective progress. Here we call for a unified language as the essential foundation for coordinated research across disciplines and effective mitigation.

records.title: Effects of forestry decentralization on rural inequality in Nepal
records.description: Decentralized natural resource governance is thought to aid conservation and reduce poverty, but its heterogeneous local effects are under-explored. A study in Nepal shows that forest governance decentralization reduces poverty but the benefits are greater for dominant ethnic and caste groups compared with minority ones.

records.title: Bridging the fuel tax revenue gap in the move to electric mobility
records.description: Governments worldwide collected US$923 billion in fuel taxes in 2023, revenues at risk with the transition to electric vehicles, especially in lower-income countries. Policymakers should anticipate and assess their own domestic exposure and develop policies to recover enough revenues from electric vehicles as the transition progresses.

records.title: The electric vehicle transition and vanishing fuel tax revenues
records.description: As electric vehicle adoption rises, governments face shrinking fuel tax revenues without clear replacement policies. This study estimates this revenue loss across 168 countries and finds that lower-income nations are the most exposed and may need international support to manage the fiscal risks.

records.title: Halving global ammonia emissions with cost-effective measures
records.description: Man-made ammonia emissions have harmful effects on human health and ecosystems, yet global mitigation strategies remain underexploited. A study now finds that emissions could be halved cost-effectively by 2050 through targeted and prioritized measures, with benefits far outweighing costs.
